title: Ordinary henselization commutes with a local quotient
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative local ring, let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be an ideal, and let $R^h$ be the ordinary henselization of $R$ [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. Then the quotient $R^h/IR^h$ is an ordinary henselization of the local ring $R/I$; in particular, the canonical map $R^h\to R^h/IR^h$ is local and surjective and identifies the structure map from $R/I$ with the quotient of the structure map from $R$.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 05WQ, Lemma quotient-henselization (lines 43616--43624): if $R$ is local with henselization $R^h$ and $I\subset\mathfrak m_R$, then $R^h/IR^h$ is the henselization of $R/I$.
